clue.text: City game doesn't end during season

indicators.note: during says the shortened game sits inside the season

parts.note: winter is a season of the year

indicators.note: doesn't end tells us to drop the final letter of the game

parts.note: chess is a board game

explanation.surface: A city's sporting fixture runs on unfinished through the season.
explanation.definitionFit: Winchester is a cathedral city in Hampshire, England, once the capital of Wessex.

clue.text: Pardon weak bowler?

parts.note: a bowler is a kind of hat, a hard felt one with a rounded crown

explanation.surface: Someone asks, puzzled, whether a cricketer bowled feebly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' suggests cricket, but here it is the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are things said when asking someone to repeat what they have just said.

clue.text: Somehow turn over flower to care for

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the rearranged word above the river
somehow says the letters of turn are arranged in some new way

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river: the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: A gardener turns a bloom over to tend it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is crossword shorthand for a river; the URE is a river in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurture someone is to look after them and help them grow.

clue.text: Keep clear diary in birthday suit

definitions.meaning: to have no engagements planned at all

explanation.surface: Someone stays home naked with nothing booked.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both having no appointments and wearing no clothes at all.

clue.text: Ruler in hospital last month

indicators.note: in places the last-month abbreviation within the hospital word

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital
ult., for ultimo, means last month in old business letters

explanation.surface: A monarch was in hospital last month.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultan is a Muslim sovereign, a monarch.

clue.text: Pulls out as minor players surround court

indicators.note: surround says the minor players go round the court abbreviation

parts.note: extras are actors in non-speaking parts

explanation.surface: Someone withdraws because bit-part actors crowd round a court.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract is to draw something out, as a dentist removes a tooth.

clue.text: Boy carries last of the metal

indicators.note: carries means the boy holds the letter inside him

parts.note: lad is a boy

indicators.note: last of picks out the final letter of the word the

explanation.surface: A youngster carries the remaining scrap of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is a heavy, soft grey metallic element, symbol Pb.

clue.text: Food can be defeated — take the top off

definitions.note: an eatable, usually plural, is an item of food

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking the top off removes the first letter

parts.note: beatable means able to be defeated

explanation.surface: A tin of food can be beaten once the lid is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a tin, but it is part of 'can be defeated'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, an eatable is something fit to be consumed, a foodstuff.

clue.text: Nuts like this are new — do try, dears!

indicators.note: new says the letters are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A host urges guests to sample some novel nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry-roasted peanuts are a common bar snack cooked without oil.

clue.text: A Republican opponent's appearance

parts.note: a rival is an opponent; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: A US political opponent makes a showing.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrival is the act of turning up or coming on the scene.

clue.text: Play about vaguely lost writer

indicators.note: about puts the play word around the jumbled letters

parts.note: to toy is to play idly

indicators.note: vaguely says the letters of lost are set out loosely, in another order

explanation.surface: A drama concerns a writer who has somehow gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vaguely' turns LOST into LSTO, which TOY goes 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo Tolstoy was the Russian novelist who wrote War and Peace.

clue.text: Anticipate facilities at Ford work poorly

parts.note: the facilities is a euphemism for the toilet, the loo

indicators.note: poorly says the letters are badly put together, in a new order

explanation.surface: The toilets at a Ford car plant are expected to work badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate something is to await it eagerly, often with pleasure.

clue.text: Prison volunteers and staff back, covered in bird mess

indicators.note: covered in says the volunteers and staff are enclosed by the droppings

parts.note: guano is the droppings of seabirds
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

indicators.note: back says the word for staff is read from right to left

parts.note: to man is to staff

explanation.surface: Prison volunteers and staff retreat, spattered with droppings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns MAN into NAM; TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: Guantanamo Bay is the US detention camp on Cuba, a notorious prison.

clue.text: Show disapproval of unfinished literary work

indicators.note: unfinished says the final letter is missing

parts.note: a book is a literary work

explanation.surface: A critic jeers at an incomplete novel.
explanation.definitionFit: To boo is to jeer at a performer or speaker you dislike.

clue.text: Make shorter queen bees get up to fly around

indicators.note: around says the word for flying goes round the bees and queen

parts.note: to aviate is to fly an aircraft
B is a bee, so two of them are BB

indicators.note: in a down clue, get up says the queen's letters rise, read bottom to top

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the queen

explanation.surface: A queen and her bees rise to buzz about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' looks like an insect beside the bees, but is the verb; 'get up' works on the queen, rising in this down clue, and 'around' wraps the flying word round both.
explanation.definitionFit: To abbreviate is to shorten a word or text.

clue.text: Inspiration for engineers in order

indicators.note: in puts the engineers inside the order

parts.note: the Bath is a British order of knighthood
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers find ideas in tidiness.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of the Bath is a British order of chivalry; the Royal Engineers are a British Army corps. 'Inspiration' means breathing in, not a bright idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspiration in its physical sense is breathing in, taking a breath.

clue.text: People packing street endure cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves the first letter of the word for endure round to the end

parts.note: to suffer is to endure

explanation.surface: Cyclists put up with the road while packing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' turns SUFFER into UFFERS by moving the S to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuffers are those who fill or cram things, such as envelope stuffers.

clue.text: Calm about Bill's song

indicators.note: about says the calm word goes round the bill

parts.note: serene means calm
an ad, an advertisement, is a bill or poster; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: Bill's tune is a peaceful one.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a song sung by a lover beneath a window at night.

clue.text: Eastern church has running water outside fence

indicators.note: outside puts the running water around the east and church letters

parts.note: a river is running water
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An Eastern church has a stream running beyond its boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fence' looks like part of the churchyard scene, but it means a dealer in stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang for a criminal who buys and sells stolen goods.

clue.text: Welsh politician's central beliefs include getting smashed

indicators.note: include says the beliefs hold the politician inside them

parts.note: a creed is a set of core beliefs
AM was an Assembly Member of the Welsh Assembly; the 's is read as has

explanation.surface: A Welsh politician's convictions turn out to involve heavy drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: AM, Assembly Member, was a member of the Welsh Assembly. 'smashed' looks like drunk, but means beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Creamed is slang for heavily defeated or thrashed, as is smashed.

clue.text: Arguments observed in live feed

indicators.note: observed in says the arguments are seen inside the word for live

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
rows are arguments

explanation.surface: Quarrels are spotted on a live news stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feed' looks like a broadcast stream; it means graze.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals browse when they nibble leaves and shoots, grazing as they go.

clue.text: Fight with the French after nap

indicators.note: after places the French article after the nap

parts.note: a rest is a nap
le is French for the

explanation.surface: After a snooze, someone takes on the French.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrestle is to grapple or struggle with someone.

clue.text: Tells teacher energy level's rising among moccasins?

indicators.note: in a down clue, the energy letter's level rises, so it moves up a place in the word

parts.note: water moccasins are snakes
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone reports to the teacher that energy is increasing in their slip-on shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moccasins' look like shoes, but are venomous snakes; moving E up a place in SNAKES gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneak is a school telltale, so to sneak is to inform on a classmate.

clue.text: Compete against Italy and Spain

parts.note: v, for versus, means against
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
E is the international vehicle code for Spain, España

explanation.surface: A team plays against Italy and Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: To vie is to contend or strive against rivals.

clue.text: Government again hires plums

parts.note: re- means again
engages means hires

explanation.surface: Ministers take on staff a second time to deal with plums.
explanation.definitionFit: Greengages are a sweet green variety of plum.

clue.text: Hands out weapons when there's room inside

indicators.note: inside places the room abbreviation within the word for when

parts.note: as means when

explanation.surface: Guns are handed out once there is space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' and 'weapons' tempt as separate pieces, but together they define the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To arm people is to equip them with weapons.

clue.text: Country song about people

indicators.note: about says the song goes round the people

parts.note: an aria is an operatic song
men are people

explanation.surface: A country-and-western song concerns ordinary folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country song' suggests country music; 'Country' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Armenia is a nation in the South Caucasus.

clue.text: Car nonsense rejected by one checking accounts

parts.note: Audi is a German make of car

indicators.note: rejected says the nonsense word is thrown back, read backwards

parts.note: rot is nonsense

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper dismisses a car claim as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor examines a company's financial records.

clue.text: Finishes features of cricket grounds

definitions.meaning: each cricket pitch has two of these, where the bowling comes from, such as the Pavilion one at Lord's

explanation.surface: A season's close is described through cricket pitches.
explanation.definitionFit: Ends are both conclusions and the two halves of a cricket ground named for where bowlers run in.

clue.text: Writer is backing poor Norse oldsters

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement

indicators.note: backing says the word is is turned round
poor says the letters of Norse are badly arranged

explanation.surface: An author supports impoverished old Scandinavians.
